accepted.sentence: Some heads carry a square drive that accepts interchangeable sockets, letting one handle accommodate fasteners of differing sizes.
A beam-style torque indicator places a pointer beside a calibrated scale; slight shaft deflection shows applied turning force.
Electronic versions may embed strain gauges in the metal shaft, converting minute elastic deformation into a displayed torque value.
Insulated versions surround the conductive core with thick molded polymer, reducing the chance of electrical contact through the handle.
Certain heavy-duty forms end in a broad striking pad designed to withstand blows from a separate hammer.
Many fixed heads angle their jaws roughly fifteen degrees from the handle plane, allowing repositioning by flipping the tool.
Some hook-shaped heads carry a projecting pin that engages holes in circular retaining rings during adjustment.
Non-sparking versions can be made from copper-based alloys, which are softer than steel and reduce spark risk.
